clue.text: Enormous Roman Stoic must get into shape

indicators.note: getting into shape means being formed anew, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: A huge Roman philosopher is told to get fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enormous' seems to describe the Stoic, but it stands alone as the definition; ROMAN STOIC rearranges to ASTRONOMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomic figures are those so vast they resemble distances between stars, hence a synonym for huge.

clue.text: Old relative given cash for food

blocks.note: a nan is a grandmother, an older relative
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Grandma gets handed money so she can buy something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Nan is the British informal word for grandmother; bread for cash is old slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a flat leavened bread from South Asian cooking, so it is plainly something eaten.

clue.text: British become paralysed after female released wind

indicators.note: what is released is let go, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
to freeze is to become unable to move
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A Briton freezes up after a woman breaks wind, a toilet-humour scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Released wind' reads as one crude phrase, but 'released' acts on the female and 'wind' is the definition: B plus FREEZE minus F gives BREEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is a light, gentle wind, so the two nouns name the same moving air.

clue.text: Famous drunken outburst about IS by curt conservative

indicators.note: a curt word is cut short, so its final letter is dropped
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the others

blocks.note: hic is the sound of a drunk hiccup
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A notorious tipsy rant about Islamic State delivered by a brusque Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest the terror group Islamic State, but they are used purely as letters; 'by' places the curtailed Tory beside them, all wrapped in the hiccup.
explanation.definitionFit: Something historic is notable enough to be remembered in history, so it is celebrated or renowned.

clue.text: Son and family at university prepare a joint

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
kin are one's relatives
in British usage a student is up at university

explanation.surface: A student son and his relatives get ready to roast meat, or something less wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts the butcher's sense, a roast of meat; the answer is British slang for rolling a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To skin up is British slang for rolling a cannabis cigarette, which is called a joint.

clue.text: List of people appearing near end of Nosferatu

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: men are people
the final letter of the film title

explanation.surface: A cast list of actors appearing toward the close of the vampire film Nosferatu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List of people' reads as a cast list, but 'List' alone is the definition; MEN plus the last letter of Nosferatu.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list of dishes offered, or of options on a computer screen.

clue.text: Vast amount of land found back in Faisalabad

indicators.note: something found was sitting inside, so the letters lie within a longer word
going back means travelling the other way, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters after the opening F

explanation.surface: A huge estate discovered somewhere in the Pakistani city of Faisalabad.
explanation.walkthrough: Read Faisalabad from right to left and the continent appears within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, an enormous landmass, so it is literally a vast area of land.

clue.text: Clerk Brit annoyed with one amusing joke

indicators.note: someone annoyed is ruffled or upset, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A British office clerk is irritated by a funny gag.
explanation.walkthrough: The irritation is the anagram signal; the fodder is CLERK BRIT plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib-tickler is informal for a very funny joke or story, one that makes you laugh hard.

clue.text: Big plan potter set out is absorbing stuff

indicators.note: to set out is to lay out afresh, so the letters are arranged in a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A grand scheme laid out by a potter makes for gripping material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbing' suggests riveting, but it means soaking up liquid, as blotting paper soaks up ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotting paper is porous paper used to soak up excess ink, literally a substance that absorbs.

clue.text: Large drink and shake maiden polished off

indicators.note: polished off means finished and got rid of, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to tremble is to shake
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A big drink, a shaky hand and a young woman being finished off, a bleak pub scene.
explanation.walkthrough: TREMBLE loses its M. In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a triple measure of spirits in a British pub, so a large serving of drink.

clue.text: Overseer primarily gets cross with language in plant

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of Overseer
a cross is the shape X
a tongue is a language

explanation.surface: A supervisor gets angry about the wording used at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' wants to be angry and 'plant' a factory; one is the letter X, the other a botanical plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxtongue is the name of a yellow-flowered weed of the daisy family, with rough leaves.

clue.text: One polite around knight being licentious

indicators.note: to be around something is to enclose it, so one piece goes about another

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I
decent behaviour is proper and polite
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A courteous person hovering around a knight turns out to be a lecher.
explanation.walkthrough: I and DECENT together surround N. Chess uses N for knight because K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent conduct offends standards of sexual propriety, much like licentious behaviour that ignores moral restraint.

clue.text: Wave of resistance milk outlet initially ignored

indicators.note: ignoring something at the start means its opening letter is left out

blocks.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a nipple is where milk comes out

explanation.surface: Protest in a dairy, where the milk shop's opening is snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk outlet' sounds like a dairy shop, but it is the teat that dispenses milk, minus its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripple is a small wave on the surface of water, so the nouns are close synonyms.

clue.text: Hedonist true to ales will get hammered

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new form

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker loyal to beer is bound to end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' is slang for very drunk, which fits the beer, but here it beats the letters into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey, the lotus-eaters lived in idle pleasure, so the term means someone given to indulgent ease.

clue.text: Chic items need reorganising in drug store

indicators.note: things needing reorganising must be sorted into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
also part of the fodder, doing double duty with the indicator

explanation.surface: Fashionable stock in a pharmacy needs tidying up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug store' suggests an American pharmacy shop; it is read literally as a place where drugs are stored at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine chest is a cabinet for keeping medicines, so it literally stores drugs.

clue.text: Red piece of tree trunk seen by Seine, perhaps

blocks.note: a caber is a trimmed tree trunk tossed in Scottish Highland games
a seine is a type of large fishing net

explanation.surface: A chunk of driftwood log spotted on the bank of the river in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Seine the French river; lowercase, a seine is a fishing net, so 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabernet, short for Cabernet Sauvignon, is a grape and the wine made from it, which is red.

clue.text: Engineers returning unopened part for building

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run the other way
not opened means the first letter has not been let in, so it is dropped

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a section is a part

explanation.surface: Army engineers come back with a sealed component for a construction job.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers of the British Army; it turns round, then SECTION loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An erection is something erected or built, such as a building or structure; the formal sense of the noun.

clue.text: Small vehicle: a black Beetle

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a car is a vehicle
taken as written
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A little car: a black VW Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Beetle the Volkswagen car, matching the vehicle; it is in fact the insect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt, so it is one kind of beetle.

clue.text: Institute opening right painterly collector's item?

indicators.note: to open something is to split it apart, so one piece sits in the gap of another

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
arty means having artistic pretensions
I is the abbreviation for Institute

explanation.surface: A gallery's grand opening attracts the right sort of artistic collectibles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Institute opening' reads like an event, but I splits ARTY after R. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectors prize rarities, scarce objects; the question mark flags that a collector's item is only one example.

clue.text: A part of a poem is deliberately wicked

blocks.note: per means a, as in once per day
a verse is a stanza of a poem

explanation.surface: A section of a poem is written to be shockingly evil.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'A' gives PER, as in 'a pound a head' meaning a pound per head.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse behaviour is contrary on purpose and runs against what is right or reasonable, hence wilfully bad.

clue.text: Turn in books confiscated by judge

indicators.note: what is confiscated is taken into another's keeping, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to rate is to assess or judge
OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Bible's first part

explanation.surface: Handing in library books that a judge has seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn in' looks like a phrase meaning surrender; 'Turn' alone is the definition. OT stands for the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to spin around an axis, so it is a direct synonym for turning.

clue.text: One fixing locks in hotel feeling spasm of pain

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an air is an impression or feel about something
a grip is a sudden seizing pain, as in gripes

explanation.surface: A locksmith working in a hotel feels a sudden twinge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixing locks' suggests a locksmith, but the locks are of hair. A hairgrip is the British name for a bobby pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairgrip is a sprung pin that holds strands of hair in place, so it secures tresses.

clue.text: On a vessel, taking a northern course

indicators.note: heading north in a down entry means travelling upward, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: Aboard a ship sailing north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container. The reversal works only because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of, so it serves as a preposition for resting upon something, as on does.

clue.text: Chap who had a brush with one punching heavyweight

indicators.note: a punch drives into its target, so one piece is lodged inside another

blocks.note: a titan is a figure of great power or importance
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man who had a run-in with somebody hitting a heavyweight boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a brush with' sounds like a scrape, but the brush is a paintbrush; I goes inside TITAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter, so a man who wielded a paintbrush.

clue.text: Island resort man fixed up close to Phuket

indicators.note: something fixed up has been put back together differently, so the letters are reassembled
the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is used

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
the final letter of the Thai resort

explanation.surface: A holiday rep on an island fixed up near the Thai resort of Phuket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as nearby, but it takes the last letter of Phuket, added to the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Montserrat is a British overseas territory in the Caribbean, one of the Leeward Islands.

clue.text: Somewhere to go around with nurse in public

indicators.note: to go around is to turn about, so the letters face the opposite way

blocks.note: a po is a chamber pot, somewhere to relieve yourself
EN is an Enrolled Nurse

explanation.surface: Looking for a toilet while out with a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhere to go' is a euphemism for a toilet; a po is a British chamber pot. EN is an Enrolled Nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in the open happens where everyone can see it, so the idiom matches publicly.
